ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The magnetic induction intensity of the uniform magnetic field is $B = 0.5 \mathrm{T}$. A square coil abcd with side length $L = 30 \mathrm{cm}$ has 200 turns, and the coil resistance is $r = 3 \Omega$. The coil rotates uniformly around the symmetry axis $\mathrm{OO'}$ perpendicular to the magnetic field lines with an angular velocity $\omega = 20 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{rad/s}$. The external circuit is connected to three fixed resistors, each with a resistance of $R = 4 \Omega$.

1. What is the reading of the alternating voltage meter?
2. What is the amount of charge passing through the coil as it rotates from the illustrated position by $30^\circ$?
3. What is the Joule heat generated in the external circuit when the coil rotates one revolution?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a square coil abcd, in a uniform magnetic field B directed horizontally to the right; the coil rotates about the vertical dashed axis OO' with angular velocity ω, and this axis is perpendicular to the direction of the magnetic field in the figure. In the external circuit on the right, after being led out from the coil, it first passes through a fixed resistor R and reaches a node; after this node there are two resistors R connected between the same upper and lower two nodes, so these two R are in parallel; the AC voltmeter V is also connected across these two parallel resistors. At the position shown in the figure, the plane of the coil is parallel to the magnetic induction lines, so the magnetic flux is zero. Reasoning and calculation: From the external circuit structure in the figure, the equivalent external resistance is R_ext=R+(R||R)=4+(4||4)=4+2=6 Ω. The coil's own resistance is r=3 Ω, so the total resistance of the whole circuit is R_total=6+3=9 Ω. The coil area is S=L^2=(0.30)^2=0.09 m^2. The maximum value of the induced electromotive force is E_m=NBSω=200×0.5×0.09×20√2=180√2 V, so the effective value is E_rms=E_m/√2=180 V. The effective value of the current in the whole circuit is I=E_rms/R_total=180/9=20 A. The voltmeter is connected across the two parallel resistors, and the equivalent resistance of the parallel part is 2 Ω, so the voltmeter reading is U=I×2=20×2=40 V. When rotating 30° from the zero-magnetic-flux position shown in the figure, the magnitude of the change in flux linkage is Δ(NΦ)=NBS sin30°=200×0.5×0.09×1/2=4.5 Wb. The quantity of charge passing through the coil is Q=Δ(NΦ)/R_total=4.5/9=0.5 C. The period for one revolution is T=2π/ω=2π/(20√2)=π/(10√2) s. The Joule heat generated in the external circuit is calculated using the power consumed by the external resistance: H_ext=I^2 R_ext T=20^2×6×π/(10√2)=120√2π J.
